To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inflammatory changes in MS normal-appearing WM are similar to those observed in the WM of non immune-mediated conditions characterized by wallerian axons degeneration, but with disease-specific features.

inflammatory changes observed in the white matter of patients affected by Multiple Sclerosis normal appearing white matter (NAWW) are similar to the changes observed in the same area in non immune-mediated neurological conditions with Wallerian degeneration (traumatic brain injury, stroke, amyotrophic laterals sclerosis, viral encephalitides), but with super-imposition of disease specific perivascular inflammation, and ongoing acute axon damage.

Inflammatory responses in MS normal-appearing (NAWM) white matter share the main features of inflammatory responses in non immune-mediated neurological disorders with wallerain degeneration, including microglia M2 polarization, but with disease-specific features, such as perivascular inflammation in the NAWM of MS patients, and ongoing acute axon damage in MS NAWMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the common and specific inflammatory changes occurring in the NAWM of MS patients.
the identification of common features and differences in the inflammatory-like changes occurring in the white matter in different pathological conditions, in particular in Multiple Sclerosis.

a comparative analysis of the inflammatory-like processes in the normal-appearing and pathological white matter in different conditions with axonal damage, with the aim to define the common mechanisms underlying inflammatory-like responses and to highlight the disease-specific characteristics of the inflammation in MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inflammation in MS NAWMs is not specific, but rather a general feature of the response to axonal damage, and that the differences between the inflammatory response to axonal degeneration in MS and non-immune-mediated disorders are more quantitative than qualitative.
the inflammatory-like changes are not specific for MS NAWM, but that they are part of a general reaction to axonal damage/degeneraton.
inflammation and microglia activation are not exclusive features of immune-mediated conditions and that they may occur in conditions of axon degeneration by non immune-mediated mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the common inflammatory-like changes in NAWM are not specific for MS and are likely a consequence of axonal degenerative processes, while the specific inflammatory-like changes in MS NWM are related to disease-specific mechanisms.
inflammation in MS NAWMs has a multifaceted nature, and that the presence of inflammation is not specific for MS.
inflammatory responses in MS NAWMs are not different from those occurring in non immune-mediated disorders characterized by axonal degeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

inflammation in MS NAWMs is a complex phenomenon, which shares with other conditions of axonal damage/degenerations many common features, but is also characterized by specific features, which are disease-specific.
the inflammatory changes in MS NWM are not specific for the disease but rather represent a general reaction of the WM to the axonal degeneration.
inflammation and microglial activation in the WM of non immune-mediated conditions is a general feature of axonal degenerative processes, which is not specific of MS.
